problem: Consider the equation ${y}^{″}-20{y}^{′}+100y=0.$ If $y={e}^{\lambda x}$ is a solution to the equation, then $\lambda =$
worked_solution:
Assuming $y={e}^{\lambda x}$ and differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,{y}^{″}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}-20\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+100{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}-20\lambda +100) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-20\lambda +100 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Factoring the auxiliary equation results in

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda -10)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

and so $\lambda =10$ is a repeated root of the auxiliary equation.
